title: 2025 budget direction and council remuneration review
subtitle: Also grants for entrepreneurs and environmental projects, a deferred arts grant list, and THEMUSEUM's funding request.
overview: The committee spent most of the meeting on the 2025 plan and budget. Staff presented an early projection of about a 12.8% tax increase for direct regional services, excluding police, and said it is a starting point. The committee recommended that staff return with a budget under an 8% increase {{vote:m8}}. Staff will also review funding to outside organizations, what services are legislatively mandated, overlap with area municipalities, and administrative expenses. A proposed 6% ceiling was defeated {{vote:m10}}.

On remuneration, the committee recommended hiring an independent consultant in 2025, with up to $50,000 budgeted, to review Council pay, benefits and staff support, with public input {{vote:m13}}. It also recommended entrepreneurial grants totalling $68,400 {{vote:m3}} and up to $90,000 in Community Environmental Fund grants {{vote:m4}}.

The Major Arts and Culture grant list was deferred to the June 19 Council meeting {{vote:m6}}. A request to waive notice for a motion on THEMUSEUM funding failed {{vote:m2}}, so that motion can be brought forward at the next Council meeting. These are recommendations that Council will consider later.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that staff return with a 2025 budget under an 8% tax rate increase, and report on funding to external organizations, mandated services, overlap with area municipalities and administrative expenses.
The committee defeated an amendment that would have directed staff to return with a budget of no more than a 6% increase.
The committee recommended hiring an independent consultant in 2025, with $50,000 in the 2025 budget and public input, to review Council remuneration, benefits and staff support.
The committee recommended staff-proposed Entrepreneurial Initiative grant allocations totalling $68,400.
The committee recommended up to $90,000 for 16 stewardship and sustainability projects.
The committee deferred the $306,000 grant recommendations to the June 19 Council meeting.
A motion to waive notice so a THEMUSEUM funding request could be heard at this meeting was defeated.

debate: Several councillors said a projected increase near 13% is unaffordable for residents facing high mortgage and living costs. One wanted a ceiling of about 6%. Others said 8% or less was more realistic given services already committed to, and noted that transit and other services support residents who depend on them.

Some councillors said the Region pays for many services that should be funded by provincial or federal governments, and called the municipal property tax system broken. Others said Council should also look at its own spending decisions, administrative costs and overlap with area municipalities.

Some argued that publishing the early numbers is honest and transparent. Another said it causes undue worry without a plan. Staff said the figures are preliminary and based on current Council-approved service levels.

A delegate from THEMUSEUM said its regional grant had not kept pace with inflation and that it relies on earned revenue. Councillors asked why the funding model had not changed, and one questioned giving money when a City of Kitchener grant already covers the organization into the fall.

On the remuneration review, supporters said a third-party consultant would be more credible and would take effect only for the next term of Council. One councillor objected to spending $50,000, and staff said they expected quotes to come in below that.
